rationale: Keep the existing WEPCO production record as the one canonical Permanent Power Company and merge the duplicate Westlands Solar Park record into it. SEC filings state that Permanent Power Company, LLC was formerly Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC and disclose a 66.7% CIM Opportunity Zone Fund interest, including the interest held through COZ 1, with the remaining 33.3% held by other CIM affiliates. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan and Aquamarine is an underlying project/SPV, not a separate manager-level company. Preserve the site's 2014 development, 2020 construction and 2021 Aquamarine operating history and retain its prior CIM/joint-venture ownership period as former history ending with the 2025 contribution into WEPCO. No third-party sale, control change or signed pending ownership transaction was found through August 19, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Westlands Electric Power Company (WEPCO)
beforeImage.description: Westlands Electric Power Company is a CIM-sponsored power platform formed to hold California renewable-generation assets. The platform is intended to sell electricity and related products into utility and long-term contracted power markets rather than operate as a regulated retail utility. Its model is asset-heavy because value is tied to owned solar and storage facilities, interconnection rights, and project-level contracting. CIM stated in 2025 that the initial WEPCO portfolio consisted of seven solar-generation facilities and one battery-storage facility located in Westlands Solar Park. CIM formed the company in 2025 from CIM-affiliated entities, and public sources do not disclose the ownership percentages of the current investor group.

milestones.event: CIM announced the start of construction at Westlands Solar Park, the asset base that would later support WEPCO.

afterImage.name: Permanent Power Company
afterImage.subsector: Utility-scale solar, battery storage and transmission
afterImage.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. SEC filings identify Permanent Power Company, LLC as the renamed former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. CIM launched the Permanent Power brand in May 2026 with 652 MW of operating solar, 360 MW/1,440 MWh of battery storage and 15 miles of transmission, plus the Grape and Daylight projects in construction or construction-ready development. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

CIM affiliates completed phased contributions of power-project interests into WEPCO; the CIM Opportunity Zone Fund interest reached approximately 66.7% and other CIM affiliates held 33.3%.
CIM Group announced the formation of Westlands Electric Power Company as the consolidated owner of its contributed California power assets.
An SEC filing identified Permanent Power Company, LLC as the former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC and reported the 66.7%/33.3% CIM-affiliate ownership split.

CIM launched Permanent Power Company as its national power-infrastructure platform and disclosed the operating solar, storage and transmission portfolio plus the Grape and Daylight expansion projects.
